title: 逃げ水 (Nigemizu: The Water That Runs Away). Heat Waves (Japanese ver.) MV-A
logline: On the last night before the girl he pushed away leaves town on the 4:52 first train, a boy who can no longer swim keeps the TV on so he won't think about 'us'. At dawn he races her train along the seawall to see her one last time, stops his stopwatch at the moment the music stops, and lets her go. Only in the last seconds do we learn that the 'sleeping' smile he saw was hers, given to him while she was awake.

story_arc.section: intro (0.00–16.98, bars 0–4; vocal + light guitar; PRESENT, 0:00 on June 16; letterboxed 2.39:1)
story_arc.beats: 0.00–2.16 pre-roll: black. A red stopwatch swings on its lanyard from the window latch. Its LCD (composited) reads 00:00.00 and catches the cyan CRT light as it turns in the fan's breeze. | 2.16–5.13 L0 'Last night, all I think about is you' (2.45): Ozu-height wide of the tatami back room behind his grandmother's corner shop. Haru lies on his side facing the old CRT with his eyes open, and the TV light breathes on his face. The fan head oscillates and the curtain inhales. He blinks once on bar 1. | 5.13–8.09 L1 'Don't stop, baby, you can walk through' (5.43): the last train of the night passes outside. Its lit windows sweep across the ceiling and his face as warm rectangles, one per beat (Light-Sweep). He turns his head toward the black sea beyond the tracks. | 8.09–11.05 L2 'Don't want, baby, think about you' (8.00): close on his left hand closing over his right shoulder, where athletic tape shows under the sleeve (his tell). Rack focus to the wall calendar: June, the 16th circled in red with a tiny swimmer doodle and 始発4:52 in her handwriting (composited, tracked). He rolls onto his back, away from it. | 11.05–14.02 L3 'You know that I'm never gonna lose' (11.39): the late-night filler on the CRT shows a heat-shimmering summer road. In the curved glass we see his reflection and, for one beat, a 10-year-old girl grinning over his shoulder: the boast she made before every race. He sits up, but nobody is there. | 14.02–16.98 bar 4: slow push into the CRT glass. The shimmer leaks out of the screen into the room (Mirage Dissolve). The drum pickup at 16.24 warps the whole frame, and at 16.98 the drop hits as a White Bloom.

story_arc.section: hook (16.98–28.83, bars 5–8; full band drops in; MEMORY: childhood, then 17; full 16:9)
story_arc.beats: 16.98–19.94 L4 光りだすロード (16.80) / L5 揺らいでくビジョン (18.20): noon, ten years ago. The camera skims 30 cm above the coastal road while the glare pulses on each beat. Nagi (10, sun-faded yellow cap) sprints past the lens toward the horizon, with Haru (10) panting behind. The whole frame wobbles with heat. | 19.94–22.90 L6 熱波ゆらり 泳いでくミラー (19.92): low on the asphalt. The 逃げ水 ahead mirrors the sky, and Nagi's inverted twin runs beneath her like a swimmer. The mirage slides away exactly as fast as she runs; the drum 16ths at 21.42–22.16 drive her stride. | 22.90–25.87 L7 光りだすロード (22.70) / L8 揺らいでくビジョン (24.15): Same-Position cut to last summer. The framing is identical, but now they are 17 and on bicycles. She stands on the pedals and laughs back at him with her hair whipping. He is still behind. | 25.87–28.83 L9 熱波ゆらり 泳いでくミラー (25.80): the カーブミラー at the pine junction. Both bikes bend through the fisheye, and they are together only in the mirror. On the fill (27.35–28.46) the camera pushes into the glass (Mirror Pass-through). The convex world turns liquid and becomes the surface of the school pool.

story_arc.section: chorus1 (28.83–52.53, bars 9–16; who she is to him and why he 'can't'; memory and present alternate, with present always on the 初夏零時 line)
story_arc.beats: 28.83–31.79 L10 思い浮かぶの君ばかり (28.99): noon, last summer. Nagi breaks the pool surface toward camera, pushes her goggles up and grins. In the soft foreground is Haru's hand holding the red stopwatch: he timed her laps. | 31.79–34.76 L11 初夏零時過ぎたばかり (31.95): PRESENT. The clock in the TV corner (composited) flips 0:00 to 0:01 on the downbeat. Haru sits up, lit cyan, with the stopwatch turning on the latch behind him. | 34.76–37.72 L12 ヒートウェイブに迷うのさ (35.05): last summer, midnight. They have sneaked into the pool. She floats on her back on a surface so still it mirrors the stars, so she floats in the sky. He sits on the edge with his feet in the water. Their reflections touch; their bodies don't. A slow 180° roll loses up and down. | 37.72–40.68 L13 君に幸せあげられない (37.75): this spring, at a meet. She touches the wall, wins, and looks first to the stands, at Haru with his right arm in a sling (injured last autumn). He smiles while his left hand grips the slung shoulder. | 40.68–43.65 L14 思い浮かぶの君ばかり (40.75): sunset seawall. She walks along the top like a balance beam with her arms out. He walks below, and her long shadow lies over him. She hops down beside him, laughing. | 43.65–46.61 L15 初夏零時過ぎたばかり (43.65): PRESENT. Haru at the open window. The lighthouse beam crosses the room (Light-Sweep). His phone lights up face-down on the sill, and he doesn't turn it over. We never learn what it said. | 46.61–49.57 L16 ヒートウェイブに迷うのさ (46.95): the wooden bus stop at noon. She has fallen asleep on his shoulder while the asphalt boils outside. He holds perfectly still so he won't wake her, and only his eyes move to her face. This sleeping face returns in bridge2. | 49.57–52.53 L17 君に幸せあげられない (49.66; drum fill 49.2–52.16): late April, through the pool-office window. Nagi reads a letter with a Tokyo university crest (composited insert). She sees him through the glass, hides it behind her back and smiles with pressed lips. This is her smile-before-tears tell, planted here for the ending.

story_arc.section: verse (52.53–76.24, bars 17–24; PRESENT and the TV; letterbox)
story_arc.beats: 52.53–55.50 L18 テレビつけて消さないように (52.60): CRT close-up. The picture changes channel on every beat (composited), re-lighting his face a different color each time. He stares at it on purpose. | 55.50–58.46 L19 僕らのこと考えないように (55.68): Beat Strobe in 8th notes. Every channel betrays him: a swim meet, a fireworks rerun, a coastal-train documentary. He flicks faster and shuts his eyes. | 58.46–61.42 L20 今日のハリウッド映画放映 (58.55): the late-night roadshow, a fictional 1957 Technicolor film shown 4:3 with grain in a painted style, with a 深夜劇場 channel bug composited. A convertible drives a cliff road above a blue sea, and he lets it play. | 61.42–64.39 L21 僕らのことまるで投影 (61.60): in the film, the woman boards a train while the man stays on the platform. An FLF morph turns the actors into Nagi and Haru painted in the film's style, and on the curved glass Haru's real reflection lands exactly over the movie man. | 64.39–67.35 L22 幸せに君なるはず (64.30): his imagined future for her, graded cool, flawless and slightly unreal. A huge Tokyo indoor aquatics arena lit like daylight; she touches the wall, turns to the board and laughs, and the crowd melts into bokeh. | 67.35–70.31 L23 僕じゃなきゃ可能なはず (67.64): the same image, now reflected in his dark window, with his own reflection standing inside it. He steps sideways out of the reflection so her picture is clear. He removes himself. | 70.31–73.28 L24 路に広がる逃げ水 (70.35): memory, noon. The mirage spreads across the whole road like a lake. Nagi (17) stands on its far shore and waves, her twin hanging upside down beneath her, her edges warped by the heat. | 73.28–76.24 L25 闇の中ではもう見えず (73.60; fill 74.76–75.49): Same-Position cut to that road tonight. Haru has walked out to the vending machine. There is no mirage, only one street lamp and moths, and he looks down the black road where she stood. The machine's glow flares (Light-Sweep) into lantern light.

story_arc.section: chorus2 (76.24–88.09, bars 25–28; the happiest night, then the turn)
story_arc.beats: 76.24–79.20 L26 思い浮かぶの君ばかり (76.20): last August's festival. At the top of the lantern-lit shrine steps, Nagi in a white yukata with indigo morning glories turns back to him with a smile. Lanterns sway and moths circle. | 79.20–82.17 L27 初夏零時過ぎたばかり (79.25): fireworks over the sea while they sit on the seawall. Each burst lands on a beat and repaints their faces. Their hands rest on the warm concrete a finger apart. On beat 3 she leans in and kisses his cheek, hidden inside a gold burst (a short White Bloom). | 82.17–85.13 L28 ヒートウェイブに迷うのさ (82.60): this May, the night pool again. A paper boat folded from the Tokyo letter drifts across the moon's reflection with the crest visible on its sail (composited). At the edge, Nagi says two words to him (her lips: 行かない), smiling and relieved. | 85.13–88.09 L29 君に幸せあげられない (85.15; fill 85.12–88.83): Haru's face as he understands that she has given up her future for him. The pool light ripples over him and his hand finds his shoulder. Then he smiles back at her: the first lie. The boat drifts over the camera.

story_arc.section: bridge1 (88.09–111.79, bars 29–36; drowning, the decision, the goodbye; drums and bass drop out 105.87–111.06)
story_arc.beats: 88.09–91.05 L30 闘えず息できず (87.86): Surface Break. He goes under into a boundless mirror-ocean (his inner world), with bubbles leaving his mouth and the paper boat and smeared fireworks above. He doesn't swim; his right arm floats uselessly. | 91.05–94.02 L31 愛とか言っていたって (90.80): seen up through the water, last summer's confession at dusk on the seawall. He says 好きだ; she laughs, shoves his good shoulder and says it back. The memory ripples and tears apart. | 94.02–96.98 L32 行くべきなのさ (94.34): June 12, dusk, the bus stop. A sudden summer shower hammers the tin roof. Haru steps out from under the roof into the rain and keeps his back to her: he is the one leaving. | 96.98–99.94 L33 ほかの誰かふさわしいよ (96.90): reverse on Nagi under the roof. The runoff from the eave falls between them as a sheet of water, and through it he is a wavering figure. He says the line over his shoulder without looking. | 99.94–102.91 L34 そりゃつらいけど (99.90): tight on his face. Rain runs down it, so nobody could tell if he is crying. His left fist trembles at his side. | 102.91–105.87 L35 君もわかるはず (103.10): Nagi understands exactly why he is doing this. She smiles first, lips pressed (her tell), and her eyes fill. | 105.87–108.83 L36 泣いてる君壊れそうだ (105.98; band out): the rain slows to 0.25x and hangs in the air. Extreme close-up as her smile breaks. The sea-glass clip glints, and nothing else moves. | 108.83–111.79 L37 さよならにも一度だけ (109.12): she walks through the water curtain and presses her forehead between his shoulder blades, once. He doesn't turn. His hand lifts toward hers and stops a centimeter short. On the pickup (111.06) she steps back and runs into the rain.

story_arc.section: chorus3 (111.79–135.50, bars 37–44; full climax; PRESENT 4:40 a.m., blue hour: the race against the first train)
story_arc.beats: 111.79–114.76 L38 思い浮かぶの君ばかり (111.93): White Bloom into the present. Haru jolts awake; he had dozed off. The clock (composited) reads 4:40, the calendar circle is behind him, and the sky outside is already blue. He is up and out of frame, leaving the empty lanyard swinging on the latch and the TV still on. | 114.76–117.72 L39 初夏零時過ぎたばかり (114.81): he sprints down the shuttered shopping street. Macro insert: his thumb starts the stopwatch (digits composited, running). Street lamps switch off one per beat as he passes. | 117.72–120.68 L40 ヒートウェイブに迷うのさ (117.72): memory pockets. As he passes the カーブミラー it flares with noon, and Nagi (10) laughs inside it. The bus stop he passes blooms with the two of them at 17, asleep against each other. He runs through circles of summer light in the blue night, and the street seems to repeat. | 120.68–123.65 L41 君に幸せあげられない (120.60): the level crossing by the station. Red lamps alternate across his face on the beat and the barrier drops. Beyond it the first train pulls away from the platform; he is too late to reach her. He turns toward the sea road and runs. | 123.65–126.61 L42 思い浮かぶの君ばかり (123.70): Beat Strobe in 8th notes (0.37 s): feet, digits, breath, the pool burst, the festival turn, the paper boat, the カーブミラー. Every cut is matched on his stride. | 126.61–129.57 L43 初夏零時過ぎたばかり (126.60): he vaults onto the seawall road. A pink line splits the horizon. The train's headlight sweeps over him from behind (Light-Sweep), and the one-car train enters frame. | 129.57–132.54 L44 ヒートウェイブに迷うのさ (129.55): side tracking at the train's speed. It overtakes him window by window, with his reflection flickering in each pane. For a few impossible seconds he keeps pace, while heat haze already rises off the rails. | 132.54–135.50 L45 君に幸せあげられない (132.55; fill 133.10–135.14): her window arrives. Nagi sits by the glass with her head resting on it and her eyes closed, a sports bag on the seat beside her. He sees her, and his thumb moves to the button.

story_arc.section: bridge2 (135.50–147.35, bars 45–48; drums and bass are gone, time stops)
story_arc.beats: 135.50–138.46 L46 君はどんな夢のなかに (135.60): click. Macro of the stopwatch stopping exactly as the band drops away, and everything slows to 0.3x. The window glides level with him; in the glass, his running reflection lies over her sleeping face. | 138.46–141.42 L47 満たされた笑み浮かべて (138.55): 135 mm on her: a small, contented smile, the sea-glass clip, blue light, her lashes perfectly still. | 141.42–144.39 L48 思い知る自分の無力 (141.43): his profile as he stops running. His hand goes to his shoulder. The train pulls ahead and his reflection slides off her face, so on the glass they separate. | 144.39–147.35 L49 陰りない君の表情に (144.35): the sun clears the sea horizon. A level beam floods the carriage and lights her face with no shadow anywhere. The window flares gold-white and carries her out of his frame.

story_arc.section: chorus4 (147.35–162.17, bars 49–53; quiet chorus with no drums or bass; dawn aftermath)
story_arc.beats: 147.35–150.31 L50 思い浮かぶの君ばかり (147.40): wide. The train runs down the coast and, in the first heat over the rails, becomes a mirage floating on water, then is gone. Haru is tiny on the seawall. | 150.31–153.28 L51 初夏零時過ぎたばかり (150.38): the stopped stopwatch hangs from his fingers by its lanyard and turns slowly, the sunrise curved in its plastic face. | 153.28–156.24 L52 ヒートウェイブに迷うのさ (153.75): he sits down on the seawall. The sea throws light at him, gulls pass, and the day's first cumulonimbus starts to build. | 156.24–159.20 L53 君に幸せあげられない (156.10): close. He cries without sound and smiles while doing it: her tell has become his. | 159.20–162.17 L54 君に幸せあげられない (159.30; the stems are nearly silent here, vocal ≈ 0 between 159.06 and 162.49): no voice. The line writes itself alone across the sunrise glare while the sea breathes, and this time 幸せ completes. The pickup at 161.44 swells the flare, and 162.17 is a White Bloom.

story_arc.section: outro (162.17–185.87, bars 54–61; English outro chorus; morning; the letterbox opens)
story_arc.beats: 162.17–165.13 L55 'Sometimes, all I think about is you' (162.30): crane up from Haru on the seawall into an enormous morning sky with cumulonimbus and birds. | 165.13–168.09 L56 'Late nights in the middle of June' (165.25): walking home, he passes the bus stop. For one beat a Same-Position flash shows the rain night, then it is empty, dry and ordinary again. He doesn't stop. | 168.09–171.05 L57 'Heat waves been fakin' me out' (168.05): the morning road starts to shimmer. 逃げ水 appears ahead, and in it her mirage at 17 on her bicycle, looking back. | 171.05–174.02 L58 'Can't make you happier now' (171.10): he walks into the mirage and through it, and it breaks like water into sparks, answering the intro's 'you can walk through'. On this downbeat the 2.39 letterbox slides open to full frame, the first time the present has been full frame. | 174.02–176.98 L59 'Sometimes, all I think about is you' (174.15): the カーブミラー shows only him. He meets his own eyes in it, nods once and walks on. | 176.98–179.94 L60 'Late nights in the middle of June' (177.12): home in full morning light, with the calendar circle on the wall. The CRT is still on, showing the film's last frame (THE END composited). | 179.94–182.91 L61 'Heat waves been fakin' me out' (180.15): he switches it off. CRT Collapse: the picture folds to a line, then a dot, and the dot becomes the sun in the window (Circle Match). | 182.91–185.87 L62 'Can't make you happier now' (182.90; fill 183.09–185.89): he slides the window wide open and summer wind fills the curtains. He lies down in the sun on the tatami and, for the first time in days, closes his eyes.

story_arc.section: outro_hook (185.87–197.72 + tail to 198.74, bars 62–65; bass gone, fading; HER side: the reveal)
story_arc.beats: 185.87–188.83 L63 'Road shimmer wigglin' the vision' (186.22): Blink Cut. His eyes close, and we cut to hers on the train at dawn, minutes after she passed him. She is still 'asleep', with the sea glittering behind her. | 188.83–191.80 L64 'Heat, heat waves, I'm swimmin' in a mirror' (188.85): her eyes open, already wet. She was never asleep; the smile was for him. Through her tears the window and the sea wobble, which is literally the vision wiggling. | 191.80–194.76 L65 'Road shimmer wigglin' the vision' (192.00): she lays her fingertips on the glass where his reflection was. Far behind is the seawall with a tiny figure on it, and along the coast road the morning 逃げ水 runs beside the train. | 194.76–197.72 L66 'Heat, heat waves, I'm swimmin' in a mirror' (194.70): the train enters a short tunnel and the window becomes a black mirror showing only her. At 196.24 it bursts back into sun, and the sea-glass clip throws a blue caustic onto her cheek. She smiles, this time with her eyes open. White Bloom, then the title 逃げ水 holds 197.72–198.74 and fades.

characters.name: 君: 汐野 凪 (Shiono Nagi), 18
characters.design: Nagi is a competitive swimmer at the town high school who has been offered a place in a Tokyo university program. She has a compact, quick silhouette with swimmer's shoulders and a long neck, and she is always mid-motion. Face: softly round with a defined chin; large dark-brown eyes with warm amber in the iris and layered highlights; straight, slightly thick brows; a small mole under the right eye; a light summer tan with a faint goggle line. Hair: a chin-length bob whose ends are lightened by sun and chlorine and flip outward, bangs cut a little short, and the left sidelock tucked behind her ear with a light-blue sea-glass hair clip. Haru gave her the clip when they were 10; it is the one piece of 'water you can hold' in a film about water you can't reach. Acting: she laughs with her whole upper body, tilts her head left when she listens, and runs rather than walks. Her tell is that when she is about to cry she smiles first with pressed lips (planted at 49.66, paid off at 103.10, 138.55 and in the coda). Colors: white, navy and aqua, with sea-glass blue (#7FD4E6) as her accent. Child version (10): the same face, rounder; a longer bob; a sun-faded yellow cap; a bandaid on her knee; a gap-toothed grin.

characters.outfits: (1) Summer uniform: serafuku, white sailor shirt, short sleeves, navy sailor collar with one white stripe, light blue neckerchief, navy pleated skirt, navy track jacket tied around the waist, white socks, brown loafers. (2) Pool: competition swimsuit, navy one-piece with a teal side stripe, white swim cap or wet hair, goggles on head, water drops; framed at upper body or in the water, never sexualized. (3) Festival: white yukata, indigo morning glory print, mustard-yellow obi, geta, plus the hair clip. (4) Departure: oversized light-blue linen shirt open over a white t-shirt, khaki wide-leg pants, white canvas sneakers, navy duffel bag, plus the hair clip (she kept it). (5) Child: yellow cap, white t-shirt, denim shorts, sandals.

characters.name: 僕: 葉山 陽 (Hayama Haru), 18
characters.design: Haru was the stronger swimmer until he tore his right shoulder last autumn, which ended his career. Now he stays in town and runs his grandmother's corner shop beside the tracks. Silhouette: tall and lanky, with shoulders that used to be square and have started to round; his hands are often in his pockets. Face: long and narrow; gray-blue eyes with heavy upper lids; faint shadows under the eyes; a straight nose; thin lips that rarely open. Hair: black, a little too long and messy, with the bangs hanging into his eyes and a cowlick at the crown. Mark: beige athletic tape on the right shoulder, showing at the sleeve. Acting: economical. His body stays still, so the camera reads him through breath, blink rate, swallowing and the jaw. His tell is the left hand closing over the right shoulder when he feels useless (37.75, 85.15, 141.43). He never cries until 156.10. Colors: navy, gray and faded black. His red stopwatch (#E5322D) is the only color he owns. Child version (10): sunburned, very short hair, always one step behind her.

characters.name: The projection: the couple in the fictional late-night film (1957)
characters.design: These are the lead couple of the invented Technicolor film on the TV (no real film, studio or actor is depicted). He wears a cream linen suit; she wears a cherry-red dress and a white headscarf. They are painted in a separate retro poster-painting style, gouache-like with soft rim light, and shown 4:3 with grain and gate weave inside the CRT. They appear only on the screen, and their one job is to morph (FLF) into Nagi and Haru painted in the same retro style at 61.60, which foreshadows the station goodbye.

characters.outfits: Woman: cherry-red dress, white headscarf, white gloves (held still, never manipulating objects). Man: cream linen suit, loosened tie.

locations: Haru's room: the tatami back room of his grandmother's corner shop, two meters from the single-track coastal line. Old CRT on a low cabinet, electric fan, breathing curtains, window latch with the red stopwatch, wall calendar (June, 16 circled), a window onto the tracks, the sea and a lighthouse. Lit by practicals only at night; flooded with sun in the outro.

The coastal road and the pine junction: a two-lane road along the shore with utility poles, wires and pines bent by the wind. A カーブミラー stands on a rusted orange pole at the T-junction. At noon a 逃げ水 mirage forms on the long straight. Used in daylight (memory), at night (absence) and in the morning (walking through).

The school's outdoor 25 m pool: lane ropes, a chain-link fence, a starting-block number painted on the deck, and the pool office with a glass window. Noon: blinding aqua. Midnight: a still black mirror of moon and stars. Night in May: a paper boat on the moon's reflection.

The seaside bus stop: a wooden shelter with a tin roof, a faded bench and a timetable board (text composited only), facing the sea across the road. Noon: her asleep on his shoulder. June 12 dusk: the summer shower and the eave's water curtain. Morning: empty.

The seawall road and the coastal railway: a kilometer where the road, the seawall and the tracks run parallel. This is the last-summer balance-beam walk, the festival fireworks and the dawn race with the train overtaking. The single-car train itself is a Blender model for exact speed and window spacing.

The train interior: a one-car local with cream-and-teal moquette seats and large side windows. Nagi's window seat holds the stage for bridge2 (from outside) and the coda (from inside), including the short coastal tunnel whose black glass becomes a mirror.
The shrine festival and the beach: stone steps lined with paper lanterns and string lights rising to a small shrine; below, the beach and the sea under fireworks.

The pre-dawn town (blue hour): a shuttered shopping street (シャッター街) with street lamps that switch off, a glowing vending machine, and the level crossing by the station with alternating red lamps and a barrier, the platform visible beyond.

The mirror ocean (inner space): a boundless body of water whose surface mirrors from both sides, with bubbles, the drifting paper boat and smeared fireworks above. It is Haru's drowning state of mind in bridge1.

The imagined Tokyo arena and the TV world: a vast indoor aquatics stadium in a cool, flawless, slightly unreal grade (his imagined version of her happiness). Separately, the 4:3 Technicolor film world inside the CRT: a cliff road above a blue sea and a little palm-lined station.
visual_style:
The look is a theatrical anime feature at 1920x1080, with present-day scenes letterboxed to 2.39:1 until the walk-through at 171.10. Acting reads at the level of a careful TV-anime studio, and light is the true protagonist. Line art is thin and colored: lines take the local color darkened about 40% and are never pure black. Faces use two-tone cels plus a soft airbrushed air layer. Eyes have layered iris highlights. Heat shows on the skin as blush on the ear tips, nose and knuckles. Backgrounds are painted at full scenic density: cumulonimbus with lit crowns and blue shadow bellies, rust on poles, sagging wires, wet specular glints on every water surface, and road paint baked pale by the sun.

Light rules:
- Memory is high-key, with a warm white balance, a 1/4-strength mist-filter diffusion, halation on warm highlights, soft lens ghosts and faint edge chromatic aberration.
- The present is crisp and low-key, lit only by practicals (CRT, lighthouse beam, vending machine, crossing lamps, train windows), with deep but never crushed blacks.
- Dawn uses horizontal light: long shadows at first, then no shadows at all on her face (陰りない).

All volumetric shafts, bloom (threshold 0.8), light wrap around characters, glints, pollen and moth motes, rain droplets and the heat-haze displacement are added in compositing, so they stay controllable and consistent across clips. A fine 35 mm grain and a gentle gate weave unify everything after upscaling.

Pipeline:
1. Anima keyframes at 1536x864 with the hw_nagi and hw_haru LoRAs, posed with ControlNet-lite (pose/depth/canny).
2. Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 for same-character variants (age 10, outfits, lighting).
3. Wan 2.2 A14B I2V or FLF at 1280x720 for acting and morphs. HunyuanVideo 1.5 (121 frames at 24 fps) where real slow motion is needed (rain at 105.98, bridge2).
4. SeedVR2 to 1080p, then RIFE to 30 fps.

Blender is used only where geometry must be exact: the train side and seawall at constant speed, the CRT collapse, and the stopwatch prop. Rule: every shot names its motion source, both acting and environment. No shot is a still image being zoomed.
color_script:
Each section's palette and light:
- intro (present 0:00): midnight navy #0E1630 and #172347, CRT cyan #6FE3E0 breathing on the faces, a single red accent from the stopwatch #E5322D. The last train adds warm sodium window light #FFB46B, sweeping on the beats.
- hook (childhood noon): blown-out cobalt sky #2D6BE0, bleached asphalt #E9E4D8, mirage silver #CFE6F2, heat-orange halation #FFB25C. Extreme contrast; shadows short and ultramarine #2A3A8C.
- chorus1: alternates by world. Memory: pool aqua #33C7D6, sky #8FD0F5, sun gold #FFD36B, white. Present: navy and cyan. Each memory beat gets a little warmer, so the alternation itself shows the pull of the past.
- verse: the room sinks darker (#0A0F22). Inside the CRT is Technicolor (cherry #D7263D, turquoise #2EC4B6, sunset #FF8C42). The imagined Tokyo future is cold white #F2F6FA with clinical blue #9FC3E6, deliberately too perfect. The final line ends almost black with one sodium lamp #E8A04A.
- chorus2 (warmth peaks for the last time): indigo night #121A3A, lantern coral #FF7A59, firework gold #FFD166 and magenta #EF476F on skin. At 82.17 it drops to moon-silver pool #A8C5DA with a black mirror.
- bridge1: inner ocean teal-black #06222B with bubble highlights #BFF3FF. The rain goodbye is slate #5B6B82, wet-asphalt reflections and the one green-white fluorescent of the shelter #D9F2E6. Bars 35–36 are almost monochrome, with only her skin and the sea-glass blue kept warm or saturated.
- chorus3: blue hour #1E3A6E to #5A7FC0, cut through by noon memory pockets in gold-white #FFF1C1, crossing-lamp red #FF2E2E on the beats, and the first pink #F7A7B8 on the horizon by 126.61.
- bridge2: the sunrise beam peach-gold #FFC98A to #FFE7B3 fills the carriage, while everything outside the beam stays blue #4A6FA5. By 144.35 her face is evenly lit with no shadow.
- chorus4: washed morning pastels: lilac sky #C9C3E6, silver sea #DCE6EE, pale gold #F6E3B4, low saturation, air shimmering.
- outro: full summer morning, cyan sky #4FB3F2, white cumulonimbus, cool shadows. It is bright but emptier: no red accent anymore, because the stopwatch is left on the sill. When the letterbox opens at 171.10 the saturation rises 10%.
- outro_hook: the train at dawn, sea blue #3D8FD1, sun gold #FFD27A on wet eyes, the sea-glass caustic #7FD4E6 on her cheek. The tunnel goes to black glass, then the final White Bloom #FFFFFF under the title.
motifs:
1) 逃げ水 (the road mirage, literally 'water that runs away'): this is Nagi. In the hook she chases it; in the verse she stands inside it; in the 73.60 night shot it is absent ('闇の中ではもう見えず'); at 147.40 her train dissolves into it on the rails; at 171.10 he walks through it; in the coda it runs beside her train.

2) Reflections keep them together; direct views keep them apart. Strict rule: the two are physically together only in mirrors. The カーブミラー (hook), the night pool (their reflections touch, their bodies don't), the CRT glass (child Nagi's grin behind him), the dark window (at 67.64 he steps out of her reflected future), the train window at 135.60 (his reflection over her face, the last time they share a frame), and the tunnel glass at 194.70, which shows only her. The rule pays off once she is alone in the mirror.

3) The red stopwatch: his role as the one who watched and timed her. It reads 00:00.00 at midnight. He starts it on the run (114.81) and stops it on the exact downbeat where the band drops out (135.50). In the outro it stays behind on the sill, so the red leaves the palette.

4) The sea-glass hair clip: the one piece of water you can hold, a gift at 10. It glints at her breaking point (105.98) and throws the final blue caustic (196.24), which proves she kept it.

5) The tells: her smile with pressed lips before tears (49.66, 103.10, 138.55, 188.85), and his left hand over his right shoulder for powerlessness (8.00, 37.75, 85.15, 141.43). At 156.10 he cries and smiles at the same time, so her tell becomes his.

6) Trains as clocks: the last train at 0:00 sweeps his ceiling; the first train at 4:52 takes her. Trains are the only things in the film faster than Nagi.

7) Circles as match anchors: sun, stopwatch face, カーブミラー, CRT dot, firework, pool ripple, tunnel mouth.

8) Running ahead and behind: she is always ahead of him in frame (childhood, bicycles, seawall). In the climax the train puts her ahead one last time. In the outro he walks forward with nobody ahead.

9) The letterbox: the present is boxed in at 2.39:1 and memory is open 16:9, until he lets go at 171.10.

10) The fictional film: 'like a projection of us' (61.60) foreshadows the platform goodbye, and its THE END is what he finally switches off (180.15).
camera_language:
Each world has its own camera grammar.

Present (night room):
- Ozu-height tripod at 40 cm off the tatami, on 50 and 85 mm lenses. Locked off or creeping at a few mm per second.
- The camera never moves unless he does ('he can't leave the room, so neither can we'). The motion comes from light: TV flicker, the train-window sweep, the lighthouse beam, the fan and curtain, his breath.
- Composition is frames within frames: the CRT, the window and the calendar box him in, inside the 2.39 bars.

Memory (summer):
- A floating, handheld-feel camera at chest height, on 24 and 35 mm lenses with low angles into the sky. Sun flares are allowed in-lens.
- The camera chases Nagi and is always half a step behind her (we are Haru). She often leaves the frame first.
- Water shots sit at the waterline, half above and half below, so the surface itself is a horizon.

Climax (blue-hour race):
- Parallel tracking at subject speed (side dolly along the shopping street and the seawall).
- A POV run with a stride bob, matched across cuts on the foot strike.
- Speed ramps that land on the drum onsets: 120.60, 126.60, 129.55, 133.10–135.14.
- The train side is a Blender plate with exact window spacing (one window per beat at the chosen speed), with the character plates composited in.

Bridge2:
- A 135 mm lens that compresses him, the glass and her into one plane. Frame rate drops to 0.3x on the downbeat. The window acts as a moving frame-within-frame, and the only motion is the glide and the sun.

Rack focus as plot: from the stopwatch to him, from his hand to the calendar, from the raindrops to her eyes.

Acting direction for every character clip: one clear intention and one micro-beat each (a blink, a swallow, a breath catch, lips pressing, eyes dropping and rising, a hand that stops a centimeter short). Big gestures are banned outside the run.

Generation practice:
- Keep each clip to 2.96 s (one bar) or 1.48 s (half a bar).
- Use FLF between two LoRA keyframes for every shot where the face must hold identity through motion.
- Use only one or two characters per frame.
- Hands are seen still or in simple motions (gripping, hovering, fingertips to glass). Thumb presses and object handling are inserts built from Blender props plus composited digits.
transition_grammar:
Each world has one fixed way in and one fixed way out:
- Present to memory always passes through a shimmering or reflective surface (devices 1 and 2).
- Memory to present always returns through his eyes or a moving light (devices 3 and 6).
- Time jumps inside memory use device 7.
- The three drops (16.98, 111.79, 162.17) are White Blooms.

Named devices:
1) 逃げ水ディゾルブ (Mirage Dissolve): a heat-haze displacement map ramps up from the bottom of frame over 1 to 2 beats, the image liquefies, and the next shot resolves out of the shimmer. Used at 14.02–16.98 (the room melts out of the CRT), 70.35, 147.40 (the train into the rails' haze) and 168.05.

2) 鏡抜け (Mirror Pass-through): push into a reflective object and come out inside what it reflects, built as an FLF morph between the mirror's content and the next full-frame keyframe. Used at the CRT (16.24), the カーブミラー into the pool (27.35–28.83), the dark window (67.64) and the train glass (135.60).

3) 光の走査 (Light-Sweep Wipe): a diegetic moving light wipes the frame on a beat and reveals the next image. Sources: last-train windows (5.43), the lighthouse beam (43.65), the vending-machine flare into lanterns (76.24), crossing lamps (120.60) and the first train's headlight (126.60).

4) 円の継ぎ (Circle Match Cut): a circle cuts to a circle at the same screen position and scale, on the downbeat. Examples: stopwatch face to sun, カーブミラー to pool ripple, firework to falling sparks into water, CRT dot to the morning sun (180.15).

5) 水面割り (Surface Break): the camera plunges through a water line, which becomes the transition edge, with bubbles and caustics carrying across the cut. Used for the pool into the mirror-ocean at 88.09, and as a rhyme in the rain-curtain cut at 96.90.

6) 瞬き継ぎ (Blink Cut): eyelids close in shot A and open in shot B at another time. It is used inside his POV, and once, finally, from his eyes to HERS (185.87). That one transfer of point of view is the film's reveal.

7) 同ポジ (Same-Position Time Cut): an identical composition across years or hours, so absence is the edit. Childhood to 17 on the road (22.90), noon mirage to the night road (73.28), and the bus stop rain night to the empty morning (165.25).

8) ブラウン管収束 (CRT Collapse): the TV switches off, the picture folds to a line and then a dot, and the dot becomes the next shot's sun (180.15). The TV-on moments in the verse use its reverse.

9) 鼓動ストロボ (Beat Strobe): cuts every 8th note (0.37 s) in which each frame is lit by a different source but matched on his stride or a circle. Used at 55.68 (channel betrayal) and 123.70 (the run).

10) 白飛び (White Bloom): the frame overexposes to white over 4 frames on a drop downbeat and resolves into the next world. Used at 16.98, 79.25 (the hidden kiss, short), 111.79, 162.17 and 197.72.

11) 静止 (Time-Stop): on 135.50 the stopwatch click cuts sound and image together. The image drops to 0.3x and the grain freezes for 2 frames. This is the one place the edit stops the music's momentum instead of riding it.

Rules: all cuts land on bar lines, half-bar cuts on beat 3, and strobes on 8ths. Lyric-onset pickups (16.80, 87.86) start the transition before the bar and the cut lands on it. Generic crossfades and glitches are never used.
typography:
Text is treated as part of the image, never as subtitles.

Japanese lines:
- Set vertically (縦書き) in Shippori Mincho, SemiBold for chorus lines and Regular for bridges. Each column sits in negative space (sky, wall, sea, the letterbox margin), aligned to a vertical in the shot such as a utility pole, the CRT edge, the shelter post or a window mullion.
- Per shot, the storyboard picks one of three slots: right third, left third, or high center. Text never crosses a face.
- Each character appears at its sung onset (from vocal_onsets.json) with a 6-frame ink-bleed reveal and a 2 px upward settle. The last glyph lingers for half a beat.

Text belongs to the world it sits in:
- Memory: a slight heat-haze wobble that settles, plus soft bloom. It exits by evaporating upward.
- Present: rim-lit cyan by the CRT and flickering with it. It exits like phosphor decay.
- Reflections: 「ミラー」 first appears mirror-reversed on the カーブミラー and flips to right-reading.
- Rain: droplets refract the glyphs.
- Underwater: the column undulates with the caustics.

Keyword rules:
- 「君」 is always the warmest, brightest glyph in its line.
- 「逃げ水」 casts its own mirage, an inverted shimmering copy beneath it.
- 「零時」 glows red, like the stopwatch and crossing lamps.
- In every 「君に幸せあげられない」, the glyphs 「幸せ」 stop at about 70% of their ink-bleed and never complete, until the unsung line at 159.30. There they complete fully, alone, without voice, then dissolve into the sunrise: happiness will come to her, just not from him.

Chinese translation: one horizontal line in Noto Serif SC Light at 38% of the Japanese size, in warm gray at 75% opacity. It fades in over 8 frames as the Japanese line begins, so viewers who need it have time to read. In memory (16:9) it sits at the foot of the Japanese column; in the present (2.39) it sits in the lower black bar, where it reads cleanly and never touches the picture.

English lines: Cormorant Garamond Italic, lowercase and letter-spaced, set horizontally low-center, with the Chinese beneath.

Diegetic text is all composited, never generated, and tracked to the plates: the calendar (handwritten in Klee One), the letter crest, the stopwatch LCD digits, the channel bug 深夜劇場 and THE END (DotGothic16 and Cormorant).

Title: 逃げ水 in Zen Old Mincho Black at 197.72. The 水 trails into a shimmer and leaves an inverted reflection, with a small 'Heat Waves (Japanese ver.)' credit in Cormorant.
signature_shots: 5.43 Last-train ceiling sweep: Haru lies awake on the tatami while the last train's lit windows slide across the ceiling and his face, one warm rectangle per beat. The red stopwatch spins on the latch in the fan wind.

16.98 White-out to noon: we push into the CRT glass, the room melts into heat haze, and the drop blows the frame to white. Out of it comes the blazing coastal road, with 10-year-old Nagi sprinting past the lens toward a mirage that slides away as fast as she runs.

25.80 The カーブミラー two-shot: two bicycles bend through the fisheye, together only in the mirror. The camera dives into the convex glass and surfaces through a pool, where Nagi bursts up grinning at the stopwatch.
35.05 Floating in the sky: at midnight Nagi lies on a pool so still it mirrors the stars. A slow 180° roll loses the horizon, and their reflections touch while their bodies stay apart.

61.60 The projection: the couple in the 1957 Technicolor film morph into Nagi and Haru painted in the film's style, and Haru's real reflection on the curved CRT glass lands exactly over the movie man.
67.64 He steps out of the picture: his dark window reflects the bright future he imagines for her, with him standing in the middle of it. He quietly steps sideways until his reflection is gone.

82.60 The paper boat: the Tokyo letter, folded into a boat, drifts across the moon on the night pool with its crest on the sail, while Nagi mouths 行かない and smiles. Then the boat sails over the camera as he goes under.
105.98 The rain stops in the air: the band drops out, the summer shower slows to a standstill, and in extreme close-up Nagi's pressed-lip smile breaks while the sea-glass clip glints.

109.12 Once more, then goodbye: she walks through the sheet of water pouring off the bus-stop eave and rests her forehead between his shoulder blades. His hand rises toward hers and stops one centimeter short.
117.72 Memory pockets: in the blue-hour street, each landmark Haru runs past blooms into a circle of noon light holding her at a different age. He runs through summer inside the night.
129.55 Overtaken: side tracking along the seawall as the one-car train passes him window by window, with his reflection flickering in every pane and dawn haze rising off the rails.

135.50 The stopwatch click stops the music: his thumb stops the clock on the exact downbeat where drums and bass vanish. Everything drops to 0.3x, and his running reflection lies over her sleeping face in the glass.
144.35 The shadowless face: the sun clears the horizon and a level golden beam fills the carriage, lighting her face with no shadow anywhere until the window flares white and carries her away.

171.10 Walking through: Haru walks into her mirage on the morning road and through it. It breaks like water into sparks, and on that downbeat the present-day letterbox opens to full frame for the first time.

188.85 Her eyes open: on the train, the girl he thought was dreaming opens wet eyes. The smile was for him. Out of the tunnel's black mirror, sunlight through the sea-glass clip throws a blue caustic on her cheek, and she smiles with her eyes open.
why_it_surpasses:
1) Story instead of spectacle. The reference is a dazzling motion-graphics and pixel-art showcase whose characters are mostly posed illustrations moved by graphics. MV-A is a three-act love story with setups and payoffs, plus a final reveal that reframes bridge2 on a second viewing: the 'dreaming' smile was her tell. Every shot is tied to its lyric line and moves the story forward.

2) Characters who act. LoRA-locked faces across three ages, outfits and lighting. Image-to-video carries micro-acting (breath, blink, swallow, pressed lips, a hand stopping a centimeter short) instead of sprites sliding across backgrounds. The client's two complaints (static shots, crude figures) are designed out: every shot names its motion source, and both leads are fully drawn throughout.

3) Light as narrative. Each section has its own light logic (CRT and practicals, noon halation, lanterns, rain fluorescent, blue hour, the horizontal sunrise). The emotional peak is literally made of light: 陰りない, no shadow on her face.

4) Edit locked to the music, including its silences. Cuts land on the 81 BPM bar grid and drum onsets. The two places where the stems go quiet are used as drama: the rain stops at 105.87, and the stopwatch stops the music at 135.50. The near-silent 159.30 line becomes an unsung line of type.

5) Transitions that mean something. Eleven named devices, each tied to a world or a story rule (mirror pass-through, the blink cut that hands the point of view to her, the letterbox that opens when he lets go), instead of decorative wipes.

6) Typography with physics. The type takes on the heat, CRT, rain and water of its shot. The withheld 幸せ glyph runs as a story thread across the whole film. Bilingual JP and CN is laid out so Chinese viewers read it easily, without covering the picture.

7) Hybrid craft where each tool fits. AI keyframes and image-to-video for acting and atmosphere, Blender for exact mechanics (the train, the CRT, the stopwatch), and Python compositing for light, text and continuity. That is the reference's own toolset, pointed at cinema instead of graphics.
risks:
Hardware not verified: this step ran in a cloud container (4 vCPU, 15 GB RAM, no GPU), and no Remote Control folder from the GPU machine was visible. Throughput and VRAM tiers below are therefore assumptions. Run gpu/hwcheck.sh on that machine, or work from a session running there (Claude Desktop, or `claude remote-control` in the project folder), before locking the shot budget.

Budget: about 78 generated clips plus about 8 small CRT-content plates (rendered at 480p, since they play inside the TV) plus 4 Blender plates. By section: intro 5, hook 5, chorus1 8, verse 8, chorus2 5, bridge1 8, chorus3 10 (the Beat Strobe reuses selects), bridge2 4, chorus4 5, outro 8, outro_hook 4.
- With 24 GB VRAM: Wan 2.2 A14B fp8 plus the lightx2v 4-step LoRAs for drafts, 20-step finals on hero shots.
- With 16 GB: offload, roughly 2 to 3x slower.
- Under 16 GB: the TI2V-5B and HunyuanVideo 1.5 fp8 fallbacks.
- Qwen-Image-Edit 2511 needs 20 GB VRAM, or 16 GB VRAM with 64 GB RAM.

Risks and mitigations:
1) Identity drift across ages, outfits and profile views. Train hw_nagi and hw_haru on 25–40 curated keyframes each, including turnarounds and the child variants made via Qwen-Edit. Use FLF between two LoRA keyframes for every face-critical shot. Keep clips to 1 bar. Reject and re-roll any clip that drifts.
2) Hands and objects (stopwatch click, letter, paper boat, TV switch). Never animate the manipulation itself. Use macro inserts with a Blender stopwatch and a still hand plate, a boat that is already folded and drifting, and cut on the action. All digits, crests, calendars and THE END are composited and tracked.
3) The train-window reflection composite (135.60) is the hardest shot. Build it in layers: a Blender train side at constant speed, a planar track on the window, her interior plate (HunyuanVideo slow motion), his running plate, and a screen-blend reflection with a Fresnel falloff. Previs it first.
4) Slow motion and rain. Generate real slow motion where possible (121 frames at 24 fps). Add the hanging rain droplets as composited particles, because RIFE over 3x smears thin rain streaks.
5) Running gaits: foot sliding and stride flicker. Frame tracking shots mid-thigh and up, match cuts on the foot strike, and hide joins with speed ramps.
6) Lip movement for 行かない and 好きだ may come out as chewing. Keep the mouth motion minimal or partly occluded, and let the eyes carry the line.
7) Style mismatch between Wan, HunyuanVideo and SeedVR2: line shimmer, over-sharpening, color shifts. Fix one I2V model per shot family, test SeedVR2 sharp against normal on line art, deflicker, and apply one unified grade, grain and light pass after upscaling.
8) Narrative legibility without dialogue. Test the animatic on viewers who don't read Japanese. The sling, the crest on the paper boat and the calendar circle must read in under a second, and the shots on those beats get extra frames if needed.
9) Originality and taste. The film-within-the-film is entirely fictional. Avoid shot-for-shot echoes of famous railway-crossing scenes; the overtaking-window reflection is our own design. The leads are 18 and the romance is chaste (forehead to back, a kiss on the cheek hidden by a firework). Pool shots are framed upper-body or underwater, never sexualized.
10) Schedule. The 11 bridge2 and outro_hook shots carry the payoff. Generate and finish them first, so any cuts made under time pressure fall on chorus repetitions, never on the ending.
